text:
maria_cs: FYI escalation from Priya at Acme — around 30 users didn't deprovision after the Okta group was removed this morning. Customer says some users still have paid seats.

priya_acme: can share logs — we removed the group at 09:12, but users are still in our org. No SCIM errors in Okta UI.

maria_cs: thanks. I asked for a screenshot of the group removal and the timestamp. Also asked for affected user list.

priya_acme: attached list (snipped): userA@acme.com, userB@acme.com — both should have been removed.

vikram_eng: looking at our provisioning logs now. I see a PATCH to /Users for each account around 09:13, but the server responded 200 with body: {"skipped": true, "reason": "conflict: duplicate employeeId"}.

jon_sre: interesting, our deprovision flow on SCIM is: when group->role mapping removed we send a PATCH that removes roles and then a DELETE if no roles remain. If PATCH returns skipped we don't proceed to DELETE.

vikram_eng: exact log line: ``[2024-06-22T09:13:07Z] scim: PATCH /Users/uid-123 - 200 - {"skipped":true,"message":"duplicate employeeId, ambiguous target"}``

maria_cs: Priya — do you have employeeId on both accounts?

priya_acme: yes — looks like a legacy import created duplicate employeeId on userA and a contractor account. We only just noticed.

vikram_eng: that explains it — our SCIM handler has a guard: if employeeId maps to >1 account we mark the operation skipped to avoid accidental mass changes. But we didn't escalate that as an actionable error in the response to the client app, so the provisioning log looked successful (200).

jon_sre: action items I propose: 1) quick mitigation: add a reconcile job that checks for skipped operations and forces manual review + follow-up delete when owner disambiguated. 2) patch behavior: return 409 or include actionable error instead of silent skipped. 3) docs: surface duplicate-employeeId caveat in SCIM troubleshooting.

maria_cs: Priya, for immediate fix can you work with Okta/your identity team to change the contractor's employeeId (or remove it) and then re-run the group push? That should let us finish deprovision. If you want our team to do it we can coordinate a small maintenance window.

priya_acme: we'll update the contractor's employeeId and try re-sync in 15m. Thanks.

vikram_eng: noted — I'll add a temporary probe that searches provisioning logs for entries with "skipped" and emits alerts; will follow up PR for response code change.

jon_sre: I'll draft runbook steps for CS to use when this crop of duplicate-employeeId events occurs. Include sample Okta queries and how to identify the conflicting accounts.

maria_cs: copying the customer success runbook item to the ticket and will follow up once they confirm resync. :thumbsup:

okta-bot: Deployment: provisioning-alerts v1.14 deployed to prod at 2024-06-22T10:05Z.

priya_acme: resync completed, looks clean now — 0 users remain from removed group. Thanks everyone!

maria_cs: closing the escalation once ticket updated. Follow-ups: vikram to file PR for error code, jon to add runbook, docs note for CS + customer-facing troubleshooting.

vikram_eng: PR filed: https://git.internal/redwood/provisioning/pull/482 - description and tests included.

jon_sre: runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CS/SCIM+duplicate+employeeID - will iterate.

maria_cs: great. marking resolved in ticket.
